answer: Clique-anchored edge weighting. Each new identity must attach to existing agents through edges that close a local triangle, so its trust weight is the minimum capacity along that thread rather than its own claim. A valid attachment also requires routing diversity across at least two independent lotus clusters, which forces the attacker to acquire real adjacency inside communities it does not control. Cost is the delta between creating N identities and maintaining N distinct, non-overlapping triangle closures, each demanding sustained participation and reachable neighbors.
